correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact decomposition Z_{k,ell}=sigma_k(n)/n^k-sigma_ell(n)/n^ell+O(n^-k). Finite prime-exponent patterns have independent geometric limiting law by CRT, while tails of local factors are uniformly O(Y^(1-k)); hence joint weak convergence is valid. Atomlessness: finite disjoint harmonic-prime blocks have uniformly positive event probability of one V_p=1 and other V_q=0; conditional resulting values are distinct because k A x^(-k-1)>ell B x^(-ell-1) for x>=2 and A>=B; maximum single value chance is O(1/min block prime). For the Hausdorff carrier, E[-log P((V_p)_{p<=X})]=O(log X); finite low-surprisal prefixes independent of the absence of primes with nonzero V between X and X^(1/eps). Mertens gives absence probability tending eps>0; the limsup low-information event is finite-coordinate-change invariant and therefore a zero-one event with probability 1. There are <=X^(K+1) prefixes whose tails are within O(X^(-(k-1)/eps)), yielding carrier dimension <=eps(K+1)/(k-1), and eps->0. Independently verified exact arithmetic normalization and prime zeros for (3,5),(3,7),(5,7), n<=199; not a substitute for limit law.
residual_risks: Relies on classical Mertens product and divergence estimates; no rate or complete topological support asserted.

value.rationale: This supplies a precise limiting distribution and the unusually strong dimension-zero singularity of a natural prime-detecting Fourier coefficient family. residual_risks: Topological support can be much larger than the full-mass Hausdorff carrier; no effective convergence rate.
